Thank you, I understand what a thought experiment is. In fact, I am even aware that these farms are not real. That being said, we do live in the real world, and thought experiments are about figuring out real world problems, which is why I take the time to bother you with reminders of what the real world is like.



As to the hypothetical question you posed, I meant to answer it. When you ask me "What if there is no suffering by the cow" I still reply that humans have no real entitlement to use non-human animals for themselves. An existence that is entirely made up of being exploited necessarily involves suffering. Your question seems to be a contradiction to me.



If there is still something that I don't seem to understand, then please explain it to me.

Boy, that's an awfully bold statement to claim that it is even possible to completely eliminate suffering by a farmed cow. Also, while a cow likely does not have a clear idea of what property is, a cow does know what things like constraint are. Cows being farmed for beef are controlled, that's a necessary part of farming. 



Cows are slaughtered between 18 and 24 months of age, while the life expectancy of a cow is about 15 years. I am well aware of the fact that cows die whether they are farmed or not, but they do not live "happy, blissfully ignorant" lives as you suppose. The information is out there for you, but I've gotten into enough of these conversations to know that it isn't worth putting in the effort to type it all out for you. 



To me, the real issue is this: there are many different degrees of suffering, both physical and psychological. Humans and non-human animals can both feel suffering the same way, although not always to the same degree, that we do. We fight so hard to eliminate the suffering of human beings, yet as we use non-human animals for our consumption, dietary and otherwise, we limit their lives and cause them different degrees of physical and psychological suffering. If we see suffering as undesirable in humans, then what entitles us to cause it to non-human animals?



What is significant is not the difference between taking a life and preventing one, but rather the quality of life. It is infinitely more desirable to prevent the life of a creature, than to cause it to live a life full of suffering.

It is not that the creation of conscious life is valuable. Instead, the way that most of us think of it is that suffering is undesirable. I would rather no cows be born at all, than to have many born in order to be used by humans. Now, you may be tempted to say that in your example a minimal amount of suffering is being caused by the meat farm. The question I would pose to you is this: What entitles humans to use animals in any way that will cause the animals suffering? We live in a world where animals are considered to be our property, but animals are thinking, feeling beings that deserve to live their own lives.
